findings.source_quote: facite igitur opera bona, quicumque accepistis a Domino, ne, dum tardatis facere, consummetur structura turris.
findings.english_quote: All of you who have received from the Lord must do good works. Do not delay until the tower is finished.
findings.issue: The source warns against the tower being completed while the recipients delay doing good works. “Do not delay until” instead frames completion as the endpoint up to which they must not wait. It does not preserve the explicit warning that completion may occur during their delay. The subsequent exclusion warning preserves the consequence but does not fully recover this clause's temporal and preventive relationship.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “So all of you who have received from the Lord must do good works, so that the tower is not finished while you delay doing them.”

summary: Both editions were reviewed clause by clause against the selected continuous Latin. The standard edition is acceptable within that scope. The simplified edition needs one localized correction to the warning about completion during delay. Both preserve the universal rescue obligation, the great-sin and blood-guilt assertions, and the life and exclusion warnings. Their notes appropriately retain the Latin working reading while disclosing the bounded, damaged Greek alternative; they do not present a reconstructed complete Greek sentence as preserved text. This review does not authenticate unseen manuscripts or certify an exhaustive collation.
